steps.observation: UsernameValidator is defined in auth/validators.py with regex = r'^[\w.@+-]+$'.
It calls re.match(self.regex, value). In Python, $ also matches just before a trailing newline, so 'alice\n' is accepted.

focus.learned: UsernameValidator's regex ends with $, which matches before a trailing newline; \Z only matches at the true end of the string.

focus.topic: Reject usernames with a trailing newline

steps.observation: 1 failed: DID NOT RAISE ValueError for 'alice\n'.

steps.action: Change the regex in auth/validators.py to regex = r'^[\w.@+-]+\Z'
steps.observation: One-line change; the character class is unchanged, only the end anchor differs.

focus.learned: Anchoring the username regex with \Z instead of $ rejects a trailing newline; the regression test now passes.
